neighbours.label: ' instead' naming what was chosen in place of something (took a car instead, tablets instead of books), as opposed to the same sentences adding something with too, also or as well
fire: The ferry was full, so they drove around the bay instead.
Our club picked a picnic instead of the usual formal dinner.
He put down the novel and reached for a magazine instead.
Most of the town now heats with wood instead of oil.
The bakery ran out of rye, so I bought a white loaf instead.
She took the stairs instead of waiting for the slow elevator.
The band dropped the ballad and closed with a louder song instead.
Farmers here grow barley instead of wheat on the upper fields.
quiet: The ferry was full, so they drove around the bay too.
Our club picked a picnic as well as the usual formal dinner.
He put down the novel and reached for a magazine as well.
Most of the town now heats with wood and with oil.
The bakery had plenty of rye, so I bought a white loaf too.
She took the stairs and then waited for the slow elevator.
The band played the ballad and closed with a louder song too.
Farmers here grow barley and wheat on the upper fields.

notes: Card: ' instead' x10 of the top 32, also ' not', ' something', ' think'. Output suppresses not/non. Probes: instead 0.31-0.42. The same pivot fires without the word: "I'm tired of black paint; I think" 0.90, 'but for the people' 0.46, 'gave up sugar and started' 0.38, while "I'm fond of the curtains; I think" 0.03. This test covers only the word; the wider pivot is not tested here.
